claims: As of early April 2026, Crunchyroll is facing multiple 100GB-scale legal challenges regarding data privacy and a significant security breach.
These lawsuits follow a previous $16 million settlement in 2023 regarding similar privacy violations.
In March 2026, hackers allegedly accessed 100GB of user data through a third-party outsourcing partner Telus International in India.
The data breach class action lawsuit claims Crunchyroll failed to properly protect user data, including emails, IP addresses, support tickets, and potential credit card information.
The data breach class action lawsuit is the second class action lawsuit in March 2026.
Plaintiffs seek damages of up to $25,000 per affected user in the data breach class action lawsuit.
Crunchyroll confirmed they are investigating the claims with cybersecurity experts.
Crunchyroll stated the issue may be limited to customer service data, not core systems.
A Video Privacy Protection Act lawsuit was filed against Crunchyroll in early March 2026.

The Video Privacy Protection Act lawsuit alleges that Crunchyroll’s app shares user data including specific anime titles watched, email addresses, and device IDs with third-party marketing firm Braze without consent.
The Video Privacy Protection Act lawsuit claims this violates the federal Video Privacy Protection Act.
The Video Privacy Protection Act lawsuit is ongoing.
Crunchyroll settled a class action for $16 million in 2023 over allegations that it shared user viewing habits with Facebook, Google, and Adobe.
The 2023 settlement was finalized in late 2023/early 2024.
